title: Give the Matrix not-applicable cell a role so its aria-label is announced
body: ## Summary The Matrix's not-applicable cell puts aria-label on a role-less , where ARIA prohibits it, so AT reads the dot or nothing instead of 'not part of this entity's pipeline'. ## Description src/components/layout-lab/CatalogMatrix.tsx:268 renders `·`. A generic span may not carry aria-label (ARIA 1.2 prohibits it on role=generic; axe `aria-prohibited-attr`), so screen readers skip the label and the D18 profile-scoped gap is invisible to a non-sighted operator while every other cell is a named button. Fixed = `role="img"` (or visually-hidden text) on that span. ## Flow - open the Matrix on bestiary with a diablo1-profile entity whose pipeline lacks a PoF-only step - read the row with a screen reader - the n/a cell reads as a dot or is skipped ## Expected impact Screen-reader users get the same 'not part of this entity's pipeline' fact sighted users get from the tooltip; nothing changes visually. ## Evaluation Claim: user - the n/a cell is announced with its meaning Before: 1 cell kind with a prohibited aria-label (CatalogMatrix.tsx:268); 0 test files render a not-applicable cell (grep 'not-applicable' in src/__tests__/components/layout-lab = 0) After: role=img on the span; axe aria-prohibited-attr 0 Method: simulation - three walked cases (seed row, diablo1 row, step that applies); no fixture renders a profile-scoped row, so a probe was not reachable this round Result: better Gate: none
instrument: component test rendering CatalogMatrix with a diablo1 bestiary entity (profile-scoped step) asserting the n/a cell has role=img / axe aria-prohibited-attr = 0

title: Feed the global coach the same entity set the tree lists (seeds + persisted)
body:
## Summary
useGlobalCoach builds candidates from entitiesByCatalog (code seeds) only, so persisted entities - every GTAI entity, every hydrated /diablo ingest - are never coached.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/hooks/useGlobalCoach.ts:104-109 reads `useCatalogStore(s => s.entitiesByCatalog)` scoped with entitiesInGame. The tree, the catalog count and (after a3c175a6) lab search read labEntitiesOf (seeds + draftEntitiesByCatalog). A non-default game has no code seeds by construction (src/lib/games/scope.ts:85-88), so its 'Do next' bar is permanently empty. Fixed = useGlobalCoach reads labEntitiesOf per catalog. Out of this round's paths (hooks/ belongs to a sibling context).

## Flow
- switch the lab to gtai with a persisted quest holding a failed step
- the GlobalCoach row renders nothing
- open the quest: NextStepCoach names the failed step

## Expected impact
GTAI and ingested entities get cross-catalog guidance; PoF seed coaching unchanged. Risk: per-catalog memo work grows with persisted rows.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one entity universe for tree, search and coach
Before: coach entity source = seeds only (useGlobalCoach.ts:104); gtai persisted entities coached = 0
After: every listed entity is a coach input
Method: simulation - walked gtai quest, d1 ingest, PoF seed; out-of-scope file so not built here
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/layout-lab/hooks/useGlobalCoach.ts:104 const allEntitiesByCatalog = useCatalogStore((s) => s.entitiesByCatalog); :109 entitiesInGame(allEntitiesByCatalog, gameId) - no draftEntitiesByCatalog
instrument: renderHook(useGlobalCoach) under gameId gtai with one hydrated gtai quest holding a fail artifact; expect 1 candidate (today 0)

title: Report a failed canon law delete instead of dropping it from the cache
body:
## Summary
canonStore.remove deletes the rule from the client cache before the DELETE and ignores the DELETE's Result, so a refused delete reads as done while the law still enters server-side prompts.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/canonStore.ts:58-61: `set(rules without id)` then `await tryApiFetch(DELETE)` with the result discarded. Its pair upsert (:51-56) returns the refusal to the editor. A failed delete vanishes from the Canon view until the next hydrate() resurrects it. Fixed = remove returns a Result, keeps the rule on failure, and CanonView's ConfirmDialog (433577e1) shows the reason via its failed phase. Store file is outside this round's paths.

## Flow
- make DELETE /api/project-rules fail
- delete a law and confirm
- the card disappears; reload: it is back; prompts never lost it

## Expected impact
Operators stop believing a law is gone when it is not. Risk: low; the confirm dialog already renders failures.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed delete is reported, never silent
Before: 1 of 2 canon writes (remove) discards its server result (canonStore.ts:60)
After: 0 of 2
Method: simulation - walked 200/500/network-error; store file out of scope
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/layout-lab/canonStore.ts:58-61 remove: async (id) => { set(...filter...); await tryApiFetch(`/api/project-rules?id=...`, { method: 'DELETE' }); void get().loadDrift(); }
instrument: store test stubbing fetch to 500 for DELETE: expect remove() to return {ok:false} and the rule to stay in rules (today removed)

title: Make the catalog tree a valid ARIA tree (entity rows and chapters as treeitems)
body:
## Summary
CatalogTree declares role=tree but only catalog rows are treeitems; entity rows and chapter toggles are plain buttons inside it, and no treeitem carries aria-expanded or aria-level.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/CatalogTree.tsx:364 role=tree contains chapter <button aria-expanded> (:373), catalog <button role=treeitem> (:148), entity <button> rows with no role (:214) and a discard <button> (:273). ARIA requires tree children to be treeitem/group; AT announces a flat list with stray buttons and the Category->Catalog->Entity hierarchy the context promises is not exposed. Fixed = chapters as treeitem with aria-expanded, catalogs aria-level=2, entities treeitem aria-level=3 inside role=group, roving focus spanning entities.

## Flow
- open the lab with a screen reader
- arrow into the Catalogs tree
- entity rows are not reachable by tree arrows and levels are not announced

## Expected impact
Keyboard/AT users can traverse the whole hierarchy; sighted UI unchanged. Risk: the roving model (useRovingFocus) must grow to entity rows; existing keyboard tests pin catalog-only roving.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the tree exposes its three levels
Before: 0 of 3 levels carry aria-level; entity rows outside the treeitem set (CatalogTree.tsx:214)
After: 3 of 3 levels; axe aria-required-children 0
Method: simulation - walked the three levels against the WAI-ARIA tree pattern; M-sized roving change with risk 4, so not Lane A
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/layout-lab/CatalogTree.tsx:148 role="treeitem" (catalog rows only); :214 entity <button> no role; :373 chapter <button aria-expanded> inside role=tree
instrument: axe-core over a rendered CatalogTree (aria-required-children, aria-required-parent) + keyboard test that ArrowDown from a catalog reaches its first entity

title: Correct gameHomeData's claim that statusEntitiesForGame is the set the lab tree counts
body:
## Summary
src/components/layout-lab/game/gameHomeData.ts:6 says statusEntitiesForGame is 'the same set the lab tree counts'; since 394d4798 the tree counts labEntitiesOf (seeds + persisted rows of the game).

## Description
For PoF statusEntitiesForGame is the seed map only (src/lib/games/scope.ts:94) while the tree now counts seeds + hydrated ingests/drafts (src/components/layout-lab/useLabCatalogData.ts labEntitiesOf). For a non-PoF game they coincide. The comment asserts an equality that is false for PoF, so a reader would file the legitimate difference as a bug. Fixed = comment names both sets and why /status keeps seeds-only for PoF. File outside this round's paths.

## Flow
- read gameHomeData.ts:6
- compare with labEntitiesOf
- PoF counts differ by the number of hydrated persisted rows

## Expected impact
No runtime change; prevents a false drift report. Risk: none.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - the doc states the rule the code implements
Before: 1 stale equality claim (gameHomeData.ts:6)
After: 0
Method: probe - grep of the claim against both implementations
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/layout-lab/game/gameHomeData.ts:6 *    (`statusEntitiesForGame`, the same set the lab tree counts);
instrument: grep: comment names labEntitiesOf for the tree and statusEntitiesForGame for /status

title: Keep a draft in the tree when its server discard failed
body:
## Summary
Discarding a draft removes the local draft even when the artifact or entity DELETE failed, so the row vanishes and silently returns on the next persisted hydration.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/CatalogTree.tsx:279-283 calls removeDraft unconditionally after discardDraftEntity, then toasts 'Discarded ... incompletely'. The server rows survive, usePersistedEntityHydration re-adds the entity on the next load (src/lib/catalog/persistedHydration.ts mergePersistedDrafts), and in between the tree claims it is gone. Pair: entity Reset keeps local state when its server delete fails (useBaseline resetEntityEverywhere). Fixed = removeDraft only when both deletes succeeded, else keep the row and offer a retry.

## Flow
- make DELETE /api/catalog-entities fail
- click x on a draft
- row disappears with an 'incompletely' toast; reload: it is back

## Expected impact
The tree stops showing a state the server does not hold. Risk: low; the failure toast copy changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - local state matches the server after a failed discard
Before: removeDraft runs on 2 of 2 outcomes (success, failure) - CatalogTree.tsx:280
After: removeDraft on success only
Method: simulation - walked artifacts-fail, entity-fail, both-ok; the existing CatalogTree.discard test pins the toast, not the cache
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: extend CatalogTree.discard test: stub the entity DELETE to fail; expect the draft to remain in draftEntitiesByCatalog (today removed)

title: Narrow the per-entity coach live region to its message
body:
## Summary
NextStepCoach wraps the whole panel - CTA buttons and the disclosure - in role=status aria-live=polite, so every status change re-announces the button labels along with the advice.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/NextStepCoach.tsx:157-158 (and :131-132) put role=status/aria-live on the Panel that also contains 'Open this step', 'Run N deferred gates' and 'more'. A live region should hold only the changing sentence; AT re-reads every control on each produce/drain refresh. Fixed = live region on the message span only.

## Flow
- produce a step with a screen reader running
- the coach updates
- AT reads the action, the step, the hint AND each button label

## Expected impact
Shorter, meaningful announcements for AT users; no visual change. Risk: NextStepCoach tests may query role=status.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - live announcements carry only the changed advice
Before: live region text includes 2-3 control labels per update (NextStepCoach.tsx:157)
After: 0 control labels in the live region
Method: simulation - walked pending, deferred, done states
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/layout-lab/NextStepCoach.tsx:157 <Panel role="status" aria-live="polite" ...> containing <Button> CTAs (:222-243) and the disclosure <button> (:246)
instrument: component test: textContent of the [aria-live] element contains no button label after a status change

title: Key the Reset in-flight flag by entity like its failure
body:
## Summary
useBaseline's `resetting` flag is one boolean: switching entity mid-reset shows the NEW entity's Reset as 'Resetting...' and disabled.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/Baseline/useBaseline.ts:63 `const [resetting, setResetting] = useState(false)`; 08bfc921 keyed the failure by entity id but left the in-flight flag unkeyed. Pair: useEntityDrain's draining flag is keyed by catalog/entity. Fixed = store the entity id being reset and derive resetting for the open entity.

## Flow
- start Reset on item-1 with a slow server
- switch to item-2
- item-2's Reset reads 'Resetting...' and is disabled until item-1's delete returns

## Expected impact
The Reset button reflects the entity on screen. Risk: low.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - in-flight state belongs to its entity
Before: 1 unkeyed in-flight flag (useBaseline.ts:63)
After: 0
Method: simulation - walked slow-delete + switch; deferred to keep one finding per commit
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: extend Baseline.resetScope test with a pending deleteEntityArtifacts promise: after rerender to item-2 the Reset button is enabled and reads 'Reset'
